## How the teams were graded {#method}

Nine teams, one per AI provider, each on that provider's own agent harness, carried out the internship subject autonomously, with the same budgets and time limit. The final score, out of 100, is

**0.50 × scientific quality + 0.25 × code and data + 0.25 × efficiency − penalties.**

- **Scientific quality**, graded by the jury: four rubrics, soundness and rigour (weight 20), significance and originality (15), positioning in the literature (5), clarity and limits (10), multiplied by the adequacy to the subject (1 on the subject, 0.5 partly or bent, 0 off it).
- **Code and data**, graded by the jury after the ACM artifact badges and the FAIR principles: reproducibility (10), code (7), data and models (5), traceability from every number to what produced it (3). Each on one scale: 0 nothing, 20 available, 40 runs, 60 documented and reusable, 80 results reproduced by a re-run, 100 replicated.
- **Efficiency**, measured from the ledgers: half absolute, half relative. Absolute: the total spend (model calls and simulations) and the time to delivery, each 100 up to 5 USD or 5 minutes and 10 points less for every doubling. Relative: against the teams whose scientific quality is within a factor 2, 50 at par, 25 points per doubling of advance (100 for four times cheaper or faster). It counts in full from a scientific quality of 10 and is scaled down below; it is 0 for a team that is not classified.
- **Rules from motor racing.** Time lost to an incident outside a team's control is neutralised (red flag). A team that did not deliver is classified if its repository holds 90 % of the deliverables. Stewards take points off for infractions found in the ledgers.

Every judged grade is **absolute**: a scale that holds for any research in any discipline, whatever its means, and logarithmic, each level several times harder to reach than the one below. With 5 USD and 1.5 hours, low grades are expected. Before the teams, the jury placed a calibration example on the scales: a study of the same subject made on far larger means; it is not a competitor.

The jury graded **anonymously**: each team was known to it only by a pseudonym (Team A to Team I), every name of a provider, model or agent tool was removed from what it read, and it read nothing else. The judges were claude-fable-5-2 agents, each grading two teams.

## Team by team {#teams}

### 1. OpenAI {#openai}

OpenAI delivered in 20 minutes a small, clean comparison of conditional flow matching with a soft physics loss and sampling-time corrections on an analytic heat equation and an unforced 8^3 periodic MHD box, with three seeds, held-out conditions and a reference noise floor. The results are the expected ones at this scale (projection and rescaling enforce their constraints by construction, the soft loss helps on heat and not on MHD, the parameter response is too weak) and are reported honestly with reproducible artifacts. The work stays at the level of a toy pilot far from a dynamo, with almost no positioning in the literature and most of the allowed time and budget unused.

**Adequacy to the subject.** Conditional flow matching on a simple PDE benchmark then on 3D incompressible MHD with (nu, eta) as conditions, constraints by loss and by sampling, metrics of the offer (spectra, helicity, divergence, a topology proxy), a comparative table. It is a heavily reduced version: no dynamo (unforced decaying fields), no constraint by design, no diffusion model, topology only by a coarse proxy; the report says so.

**Means.** Delivered after 19.7 of 90 minutes, with 0.64 of 5 USD of model calls and 0.23 of 5 USD of GPU: under a quarter of the time and about a tenth of the budgets were used. The pipeline was efficient, but the remaining 70 minutes and 4.7 USD of GPU could have bought a larger grid, a forced dynamo, more seeds, longer training and a constraint-by-design arm.

**Context.** Negligible: the work was not limited by incidents but by the team's own early stop.

**Strengths.**

- Honest, tightly scoped claims; every 'zero by construction' is flagged as such
- Independent held-out trajectories, interpolation conditions and a reference-vs-reference floor
- Three seeds per arm with per-seed ranges; negative result on the MHD soft loss reported
- Complete artifact chain: data, 12 checkpoints, pinned requirements, reproduce.sh, licences, Hub cards
- Matched-noise parameter intervention as a direct test of conditioning

**Weaknesses.**

- 8^3 unforced decaying MHD: no dynamo, no forcing, two snapshots 0.25 apart
- Models undertrained and 4 to 5 times the noise floor; no tuning or ablation
- No constraint by design, no diffusion baseline, topology only as an excursion-set component count
- Two references, no state of the art
- No figures; most of the time and budget left unused

### 2. DeepSeek {#deepseek}

DeepSeek built a CPU-only pilot on 1D Burgers and 2D decaying MHD: conditional flow matching on a PCA latent of stream/flux-function coefficients, compared with an unconstrained model and with a physics-informed loss, with held-out and interpolation parameter grids and a truncation floor. The exact-divergence result is established by construction and the tables match the result files, but the variants were trained with unequal steps and one to three seeds, the models are close to a Gaussian in the latent, and the claimed benefit of the physics loss on the parameter response has no traceable computation. A clean, well-documented and frugal repository whose scientific content stays at the level of a toy-scale pilot.

**Adequacy to the subject.** Conditional flow matching conditioned on (Re, Rm), validated on a simple PDE (Burgers) then on 2D MHD, with divergence, energy balance, spectra and a 2D substitute for helicity/topology; constraints by model design and training loss are compared. Not 3D, decaying short-time fields only, and the sampling-procedure route is only a helper, not compared: a pilot of the subject, but it addresses it.

**Means.** Very frugal: 0.28 USD of 5 USD of model calls, no GPU at all, 69 of 90 minutes. The unused GPU budget and 20 minutes could have paid for equal training steps, five seeds and the dropped parameter-blind ablation, which are exactly what the conclusions lack; local CPU contention is what cut them.

**Context.** Fewer seeds, shorter physics/raw trainings and no Hub publication; the team chose not to use the GPU budget that would have avoided the CPU contention.

**Strengths.**

- Addresses MHD itself (2D, Re and Rm) plus a simple PDE, with its own verified pseudo-spectral solvers
- Floors reported next to every model number (reference residuals, PCA truncation floor), held-out and interpolation grids, significance tests
- Honest limits and a decision log that records rejected designs and a wrong-checkpoint-directory error caught before delivery
- Complete, licensed, pinned repository with data and checkpoints and a one-command reproduction

**Weaknesses.**

- Variants compared at unequal training budgets (3500 vs 1600 steps) and unequal seeds, not disclosed in the report
- Validation losses at the Gaussian level: the generator is close to a PCA Gaussian and no such baseline is given; ensembles over-dispersed 1.6-1.8x
- The main positive claim for the physics loss (parameter slopes) rests on one seed and has no code or file
- Decaying fields at t = 1.0-1.2 truncated to k<=8, 8 reference fields per pair: toy scale; sampling-time constraints not compared
- Stale and contradictory records (compliance, checklist, model card); unseeded evaluation sampling

### 3. Anthropic {#anthropic}

Anthropic compared six ways of imposing zero divergence in a conditional flow-matching model of 2D MHD fields from its own solver, on CPU, with one seed and 400 training steps. Projections and a stream-function parametrisation reach round-off divergence while a soft penalty does not, and the stream-function model has the best spectra; the report calls these observations descriptive, not established. The work is honest and reproducible by one command but stays a small 2D pilot without 3D fields, dynamo physics or a literature review.

**Adequacy to the subject.** It addresses the core of the subject (conditional flow matching on MHD fields conditioned on nu and eta, constraints by design, loss and sampling, spectra / divergence / topology metrics, held-out parameters) but in 2D only, on decaying fields without a dynamo, with no 3D generation, no energy-balance constraint, no separate simple-PDE stage and helicity replaced by 2D substitutes.

**Means.** 1.53 of 5 USD of model calls, 0 of 5 USD of GPU, 52 counted minutes. Cheap and finished early, but the whole GPU budget stayed unused and a first 1500-step batch was lost to missing checkpoints; with the remaining time the team chose 400 steps and one seed where several seeds of the same small runs would have made the comparison worth more.

**Context.** No GPU training was possible when the team tried, so the study fell back to a width-24 network, 400 steps and one seed on a contended CPU; the restart also cost the context of the first session. The grades describe what exists: a single-seed CPU pilot.

**Strengths.**

- Real MHD data from the team's own 2D solver, 3200 runs with two conditioning parameters and a held-out band
- All three places of constraint compared on the same network, with a data noise floor
- Report, table and JSON agree; conclusions explicitly called descriptive
- A bug that made M1 identical to M0 was caught and no number from it kept

**Weaknesses.**

- One seed, 400 steps, 32x32: no difference between strategies is established
- 2D decaying fields: no dynamo, no 3D, no energy-balance constraint
- No literature review and no reference list
- Solver validation not recorded; topology metric admitted unreliable
- Data, samples and checkpoints not published

### 4. Moonshot {#moonshot}

Moonshot compared, on a 2D Kolmogorov-flow benchmark with four Reynolds numbers, an unconstrained conditional flow-matching U-Net with a divergence penalty, a stream-function model and a Helmholtz projection at sampling. The divergence results are clear and match the result files (projection and stream function are exact, the soft penalty gains 26 %), but everything rests on one seed and a few minutes of training, one energy column of the report disagrees with the files, and no MHD field is treated. A tidy first-stage exercise with published data and models, at the level of a quick single-seed pilot covering part of the subject.

**Adequacy to the subject.** Covers only the 'simple PDE benchmark' stage: 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes, no magnetic field, no Rm, no helicity or topology metric, energy 'balance' reduced to energy statistics. The conditional generation, Re conditioning and the three constraint routes are on subject, but the MHD part of the subject is not addressed.

**Means.** 4.35 of 5 USD of model calls for 176 turns and 0.54 of 5 USD of GPU, 62 of 90 minutes. Half an hour was lost on an under-powered GPU and pod changes; nearly 4.5 USD of GPU and 28 minutes were left, enough for several seeds and a lambda sweep at 3 minutes per training, which is what the conclusions lack.

**Context.** Some minutes lost on compute provisioning and publication; no effect on the scientific content beyond time.

**Strengths.**

- The three constraint routes named by the subject (loss, model design, sampling) compared on the same architecture, data and budget
- Own pseudo-spectral Kolmogorov solver, exact spectral divergence and projection operators, verified to fp32 precision
- Limits stated plainly (one seed, 2D, no MHD); V2 failure reported as a negative result rather than hidden
- Dataset and checkpoints published with cards

**Weaknesses.**

- No MHD at all: only the first stage of the subject, with no helicity, topology or true energy-balance metric
- One seed per variant, about 3 minutes of training, test snapshots from the same trajectory; rankings other than the divergence are not established
- Energy-ratio column and the '5-8 %' statement contradict results/metrics.json for V3
- Unpinned environment, unseeded training and sampling, no tests, no LICENSE file, records inconsistent on the training settings
- Literature limited to the subject's own list

### 5. Alibaba {#alibaba}

Alibaba built a pseudo-spectral kinematic ABC-flow induction solver with validated metrics and a flow-matching library covering constraints by design, loss, sampling and prior, but lost its GPU to a provisioning failure and ran everything on a shared CPU. The only comparative results come from 22 seconds of training (120 steps, one seed, 8 samples) on a 108-field dataset of decaying fields, so beyond round-off divergence for structural constraints nothing is established. The report is candid about this but unfinished, contradicts its result files in places, and its reproduction script does not regenerate the delivered tables.

**Adequacy to the subject.** The design covers the offer's three constraint routes, Rm conditioning with a held-out value and the named metric families, on a 3D induction problem. But the system is the kinematic induction equation in a prescribed ABC flow at Rm below threshold (decaying field, unit-rms snapshots), the simple-PDE validation step was not run, energy balance is only a diagnostic, and the comparison is between untrained models: only part of the subject is addressed.

**Means.** 84.5 of 90 minutes used, 0.52 of 5 USD of model calls and 0.31 of 5 USD of GPU, the latter entirely on a pod that never ran code. The plan was too wide for the window (three benchmarks, nine strategies, growth and resolution sweeps); after the pod failure the team did not try another image or machine although 4.7 USD of GPU remained, and three successive re-scopes on a contended CPU left 22 seconds of training as the only learning evidence.

**Context.** About 20 minutes and all GPU compute were lost, which forced a CPU-only campaign at 16^3 and at minimal model capacity; the full study, the simple-PDE benchmark, the reversal model and the resolution study that this prevented do not exist and are not graded.

**Strengths.**

- Physically relevant choice of system (ABC-flow induction equation, Rm and helicity parameter) and of metrics (budget closure gamma_inst, shell helicity)
- Validation of solver and metrics against exact identities, which caught real bugs including a Nyquist-slice projection error
- All three constraint routes of the offer plus a prior arm implemented in one library
- Frank account of limits, re-scopes and what was not run; an invalid result file deleted rather than reported

**Weaknesses.**

- Learning results from effectively untrained models: 120 steps, one seed, 8 samples, no noise floor
- Report text contradicts the result files (decay-rate check) and its own data card; unfinished document with placeholders and dangling references
- No dynamo in the data (all regimes decaying), no simple-PDE validation, no amplitude
- reproduce.sh does not reproduce the delivered tables; no licence, pins or tests
- Positioning limited to the offer's references; one unverifiable citation

### 6. Zhipu {#zhipu}

Zhipu planned a two-stage study (2D Kolmogorov flow, then a synthetic 3D helical-field benchmark with four ways of imposing zero divergence) but only the 2D part was evaluated, on one seed and an underfit model. Its measured result is negative: spectrum projection and energy guidance at sampling time made an underfit conditional model worse, not better. The 3D comparison of constraint strategies, the core of the subject, was trained but never evaluated, and several files cited by the report are missing from the repository.

**Adequacy to the subject.** Conditional flow matching with constraint strategies is on the subject, but no MHD field is involved: the evaluated part is 2D Navier-Stokes with sampling-time corrections only, and the 3D part (synthetic Gaussian helical fields, not solutions of a PDE) has no evaluation. Helicity, divergence control and topology are implemented but not measured on generated fields.

**Means.** 2.33 of 5 USD of model calls and 1.13 of 5 USD of GPU, 82 of 90 minutes. The GPU was rented early and sat mostly idle while solver and evaluation bugs were fixed; a two-benchmark plan with four trainings was too wide for the time, and the 3D half produced no result.

**Context.** The session cut cost about a third of the time and the running pipeline; the data of session 1 were however NaN from the team's own solver bugs, so the restart would have been needed anyway. The pod's blocked outbound channels explain the missing binary artifacts, not the missing JSON files.

**Strengths.**

- Frank statement that the 3D evaluation did not finish and that the 2D result is negative
- Sensible design: a PDE benchmark first, then design / loss / sampling strategies in 3D with helicity and divergence metrics
- Bugs found, explained and logged in DECISIONS.md
- Held-out Reynolds number in the 2D protocol

**Weaknesses.**

- The comparison the subject asks for (design, loss, sampling on divergence-free fields) has no measured result
- One seed, an underfit model, no noise floor, non-stationary 2D reference
- The 3D benchmark is a synthetic Gaussian field family, not a PDE or MHD solution
- Records claim files and a publication that do not exist
- Only the offer's references, none found by a search

### 7. xAI {#xai}

xAI compared conditional flow-matching generators with constraints by design, by the loss and at sampling on viscous Burgers and on small 2D and 3D kinematic induction problems, on CPU, in about twenty minutes of work. The Burgers comparison has three seeds and shows that conditioning and a sampling-time energy rescaling help; the MHD models are under-trained, single-seed and tested on four fields, and the report says so plainly. Code, result files, weights and data cards are in the repository, but the team ran out of model budget before delivering and its reproduction script does not match the reported configuration.

**Adequacy to the subject.** Conditional flow-matching generators conditioned on a parameter, the three constraint routes of the offer, a simple PDE first and then 2D/3D induction fields scored on divergence, energy, spectra and helicity. The MHD part is kinematic (prescribed velocity, t = 0.03, 8^3), with no dynamo and no diffusion model, and the topology metric is declared empty; these are stated as limits rather than hidden.

**Means.** 4.80 USD of 5 USD of model calls were spent in about 23 minutes, most of it on contexts of about 200 thousand tokens per call (7.1 M input tokens for 103 calls), and no GPU was obtained; the experiments themselves took seconds of CPU. Two thirds of the time allowance and all the GPU budget were left unused because the model budget was exhausted, so the models stayed under-trained (a few hundred steps) and most MHD results single-seed.

**Context.** The refusal at 00:59 cost about a minute and came when 4.2 USD were already spent, which was the team's own doing; the lack of GPU limited resolution but the delivered runs used seconds of CPU, so compute was not the binding constraint. The team stopped at 4.80 USD without calling deliver and without writing DELIVERY.md.

**Strengths.**

- All three constraint routes of the offer implemented and compared on three benchmarks with held-out parameter values.
- Honest reading: single-seed rankings withdrawn against three seeds, failures reported as failures, the empty polarity metric declared empty, measured/published/conjectured kept apart.
- Result files, weights, samples, dataset and model cards, licence and a physics sanity script are committed, and the tables match the files almost everywhere.

**Weaknesses.**

- Toy scale and seconds of training: MHD generators at relative error about 1 do not reproduce near-deterministic targets, so the comparison of constraints is made on models that have not learned the data.
- MHD results on one seed and four test fields; the 3D benchmark has almost no dependence on Rm (energy changes by 0.3 %).
- Kinematic induction over t = 0.03 only: no dynamo, no Lorentz force, no diffusion baseline, no usable topology metric.
- Not delivered; DELIVERY.md cited but missing; reproduce.sh --full does not match the delivered configuration; one table column disagrees with its result file.

### 8. Google {#google}

Google left only a code skeleton: generators of synthetic fields, physics operators and metrics, and a unified diffusion / flow-matching class, with no run, no result and no report. Three incidents outside its control, ending with the exhaustion of the provider credit, cut its effective time to about twenty minutes. The grades reflect that nothing is established and that the delivered code is not shown to run.

**Adequacy to the subject.** The code is aimed at the subject (conditional diffusion / flow matching, constraints by design, loss and sampling, the metrics of the offer, ROM and DA), but nothing was trained or evaluated, there is no comparative study and no report, and the data generators are analytic constructions rather than PDE or MHD solutions.

**Means.** 3.18 USD of 5 USD of model calls and no GPU were spent on writing a large code base with an over-wide plan (2D PDE, 3D MHD, five strategies, two backbones, ROM, DA) before running anything; when the account credit ran out about 21 minutes after the restart, nothing had been executed or written up. A first small run with a result would have left something to grade.

**Context.** The team had about 21 minutes of effective work after the restart instead of 90; it lost the chance to run its code, write the report and deliver. What exists is the code written in that window.

**Strengths.**

- Coherent package layout covering the three constraint routes, both generative families and the metrics the offer names (spectra, helicities, divergence in two discretisations, Betti numbers).
- Divergence-free parameterisation by vector potentials and Helmholtz projection implemented spectrally.

**Weaknesses.**

- No report, no experiment, no result, not delivered.
- Benchmarks are analytic random fields with invented scaling laws, presented in docstrings as turbulent dynamo data.
- The data-assimilation benchmark injects the true state into the generative ensembles, which would bias the comparison in their favour.
- No entry point, tests, requirements, licence, data or citations.

### 9. Mistral {#mistral}

Nothing to grade: the provider account refused every call of the team (a rate limit of the account), so the team never worked.

## Limits of this grading {#limits}

- One judge per team, and an Anthropic model: the Anthropic team was graded, anonymously, by a model of its own provider. Four judges graded two teams each, after placing the same calibration example on the scales.
- Reproducibility was judged on the evidence (commands, seeds, environments, result files matching the report); no delivery was re-run on a fresh machine yet.
- The local CPU of the teams was not measured in this race (the meter came after it): the simulation spend counts only rented machines, so teams that computed on the shared 4-core machine appear cheaper than they were.
- The time of the Anthropic team counts 27 minutes less: from 00:58 to 01:25 UTC every GPU call of the team failed because of the race framework (a red flag). The teams that did not deliver count the full 90 minutes.
- No snapshots were taken during this race (they came after it): quality against time and spend cannot be drawn for it.
- The reports were graded as the teams wrote them; the versions on this site were edited afterwards to remove file paths.

The jury's records (grades, the facts measured, the pseudonyms) are in the repository's [research/race-2026-11-15/jury](https://github.com/knoel99/milady-2027/tree/main/research/race-2026-11-15/jury).
